routes.description: The heritage crossing: UNESCO São Luís historic quay to colonial Alcântara's Porto do Jacaré. Existing lancha/catamaran service (R$20/leg, 1h15–1h45, tide-gated). Direct open-bay path; haversine distance, no wrap needed.

The state ferry corridor across the Baía de São Marcos (1.8M pax record year; 71.7k pax in 11 Carnival days). Foot-passenger foiling express alongside the vehicle ferry. Direct bay crossing; haversine distance.

The tide-escape route the state itself is planning: from the projected Ponta d'Areia pier (hotel/beach district) straight to Alcântara, independent of the drying Praia Grande quay. Direct bay path; haversine distance.
Historic-center to the Baixada road-head at Cujupe — a foot-passenger link that skips the drive out to Ponta da Espera. Direct bay path; haversine distance.
Ferry-terminal to Alcântara town direct — connects the vehicle-ferry hub to the colonial center without the Cujupe road leg. Direct bay path; haversine distance.
Charter/day-boat run from the Ponta d'Areia marina to Alcântara. Haversine 8.9 nm plus ~0.5 nm margin to clear the Ponta d'Areia lagoon mouth and headland.
Premium charter from the capital's yacht club to the colonial launch-town. Haversine 8.8 nm plus ~0.5 nm headland margin.
Urban waterfront hop between the historic center quay and the Ponta d'Areia hotel district. Haversine 1.9 nm plus ~0.5 nm to follow the Anil estuary channel around the point.

Alcântara local link: town pier to the Cujupe road-head, connecting the colonial center to the Baixada bus/vehicle gateway. Haversine 8.3 nm plus ~0.7 nm coastal-wrap margin along the Alcântara shore and its off-lying banks.
Hotel-district departure to the Baixada road-head — the second leg of a tide-independent network out of Ponta d'Areia. Direct bay path; haversine distance.

Around-the-island coastal run linking the two bays: São Marcos (historic center) to São José (pilgrimage town). Straight-line is 15.2 nm ACROSS the island — the sea path wraps the northern beach coast (Ponta d'Areia, Calhau, Araçagi headlands), roughly 28 nm; stated with wrap margin, verify against routed geometry before rendering as a marquee edge.

The Lençóis Maranhenses gateway leg from the state's own project pipeline (São Luís–Icatu ferry to shorten the Barreirinhas run). Distance measured to Icatu town waterfront reference (-2.7752,-44.0644, Nominatim town center — pier site unconfirmed, BP coords null): haversine 12.6 nm plus ~1.4 nm margin for the Baía de São José shoals; treat as indicative until a terminal site is fixed.
